title: On a time-oriented globally hyperbolic four-dimensional spacetime, Lorentzian distance is the infimum of positive causal-function increments under the global past-directed timelike eikonal bound
author: Nicolas Franco
work: Global Eikonal Condition for Lorentzian Distance Function in Noncommutative Geometry
source_version: Official SIGMA 6 (2010) article 064, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2010.064; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256

source_locator.theorem: Theorem1 continuous causal-function Lorentzian distance formula
source_locator.label: mainth

difficulty_reason: The reverse Cauchy-Schwarz inequality gives only one direction of the distance formula; obtaining the infimum requires global functions approximating a prescribed pair of points while satisfying a timelike bound everywhere. The author builds locally finite causal-cone covers of a Cauchy hypersurface and sums Lorentzian point-distance functions outside the protected region. Separate comparable and incomparable constructions combine past and future support controls to recover both the positive distance and its zero branch.

proof_review.note: Read full time-orientation/signature and reverse-Cauchy-Schwarz lower bound3-4, the chosen space A of continuous causal functions and its monotone-along-causal-path integration inequality4, precisely cited global-hyperbolicity/distance/cut-locus/Cauchy-surface foundations5-6, full new locally finite cone-cover and distance-sum construction Lemma4 on6-7, and complete comparable/incomparable endpoint approximation Lemmas5/6 and intervening corollaries7-10. Select Theorem1 in the explicitly fixed continuous causal-function setting on a time-oriented globally hyperbolic4-dimensional spacetime of signature(-,+,+,+). Candidate functions obey the source almost-everywhere gradient convention, global essential upper bound g(grad f,grad f)<=-1 and past-directed gradient. The resulting infimum of max(0,f(q)-f(p)) is the directed Lorentzian distance, including incomparable and reversed pairs. The source Notes10 discuss a different absolutely-continuous-function extension and acknowledge an additional distance-function regularity proof would improve that extension; no such unproved extension, smooth-test-function replacement, operator/noncommutative formula or every-dimension generalization selected. Standard causal geometry and the precise Bernal-Sanchez Cauchy hypersurface theorem are named foundations; the new support/cover/approximation cores are present. Exact selected statement and terminal proof pages rendered and visually inspected; physical headers/native ZIP members and source/license hashes checked. No independent mathematical reproof.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Theorem1 in its fixed A=continuous causal functions setting, on an oriented and time-oriented globally hyperbolic four-dimensional spacetime with metric signature(-,+,+,+). For all p,q, directed Lorentzian distance d(p,q) equals inf_f max(0,f(q)-f(p)), where admissible continuous causal f have the source almost-everywhere defined gradient, essSup_M g(grad f,grad f)<=-1 and past-directed gradient. No replacement of A by arbitrary Sobolev/absolutely continuous or smooth test functions, no noncommutative/operator distance formula, and no removal of global hyperbolicity.
original_metadata.editorial_warning: The separate Notes10 extension to other function spaces requests additional absolute-continuity regularity of point-distance functions. The selected claim retains the original continuous causal-function class and its stated monotone path inequality; no extra extension or repaired regularity argument is supplied.
